shorts.title: What you will learn: for loops
shorts.hook: One line holds the whole loop: start, test and step.
shorts.script: One line holds the whole loop: start, test and step. Today we meet the for loop. It packs the start, the test and the step into one tidy line. A for loop has three parts in its round brackets. First, the start. It runs once. Second, the test. It runs before each round. Third, the step. It runs after each round. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: for loops.

shorts.title: for loops in one minute
shorts.hook: A for loop has three parts in its round brackets.
shorts.script: A for loop has three parts in its round brackets. First, the start. It runs once. Second, the test. It runs before each round. Third, the step. It runs after each round. A variable made in the start belongs only to the loop. Think of a bus route. You begin at the first stop, check if there is a next stop, and move on. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: for loops in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: The body prints one row of the table.
shorts.script: The body prints one row of the table. The loop makes five rows. A second loop counts down. It starts at three. The step is k minus minus. It prints three, two and one. Then endl ends the line. The table of seven prints five rows. Then the line, three two one, appears. A for loop holds the start, the test and the step in one line. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A semicolon after the for
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. A semicolon sits after the for line. That is an empty body. The loop spins five times and does nothing. Then the block runs only once. The compiler warns about the empty body. Remove the semicolon. The semicolon is an empty loop body. The loop runs five times and does nothing. The block below then runs once. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A SEMICOLON AFTER THE FOR
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A semicolon after the for.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Why do for loops make good friends? They always count on you.
shorts.script: Why do for loops make good friends? They always count on you. Use a for loop to print the even numbers from two to twenty. Write your answer in the comments. A for loop holds the start, the test and the step in one line. The start runs once, and the step runs after each round. Count down with minus minus. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
